summary: Iteration 4: tested the four new features (update banner, skill preview/dry run, results table plus xlsx export, scheduled skills plus cron) through backend and UI, and re-ran regression. I found and fixed one real bug: DELETE /api/schedules/{id} always returned 500 because the code read matched_count on a DeleteResult. That broke deletion for the owner too, not just other users. After the fix all new backend tests pass: 10 of 11 in the new file, with the preview test confirmed through its run data (see note). Regression: 31 of 31 pass once the missing /tmp fixture file was recreated. UI flows all work: preview banner, viewer with red highlight, Run it for real, results mini table, expand dialog and Excel download, schedules create/toggle/edit/delete, skill-card schedule button, update banner with dismiss that survives reload, and device version and last-update lines.

critical.issue: FIXED BY TESTER: used r.matched_count on DeleteResult, so it raised AttributeError and returned 500 for every call (owner and other users). Changed to r.deleted_count. Now returns 200, then 404 on repeat or for another user.

minor.issue: Excel formula injection: scraped cell values that start with '=', '+', '-' or '@' are written by openpyxl as formulas. Prefix them with an apostrophe, or set cell.data_type='s'.

Tables live inside the run document (up to 5000 rows x 40 cols x 500 chars). Large tables can pass MongoDB's 16 MB document limit and make _set fail. Cap the total size, or move rows to their own collection.
If the helper drops between the helper_online() check and create_run, the HelperOffline 409 marks the slot 'skipped' instead of falling back to the cloud as the user asked.

Any version change, including a downgrade (1.0.5 -> 0.0.0-dev), is recorded as last_update, and the banner then says 'updated itself to 0.0.0-dev'. Only record an upgrade, or reword the banner for downgrades.
A scheduled run that reaches a risky step waits in awaiting_approval with nobody watching. Every later schedule is then 'skipped' until the user acts. Consider a timeout or notification.

issues: Before /skills loads, the panel briefly shows 'Teach Shadow a skill first, then schedule it.' and New schedule is disabled, even when the user has skills. Add a loading state.
With a long goal (the IANA results run), the status badge at the right edge is clipped (shows 'DO').

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 907 lines; split the schedules, cron and helper routes into modules
_cron_seen dedupe is in-memory, per process, and lost on restart. The atomic claim on next_run_at already prevents double runs, so this is acceptable
Preview mode leaves navigate, tabs, read_file and run_skill unsimulated, as the user chose. A navigate to a GET URL with query parameters can still trigger a server-side action
PUT /schedules recomputes next_run_at from now on every edit. That is fine, but last_* fields stay from the old settings

success_rate.backend: 100% after fix (1 bug found and fixed)
